description: Trust-tier expectations for the System Health renderers (T-E2 conformance seed, chipmunk R3 2026-11-10). LANGUAGE-NEUTRAL DATA: any surface implementation (verify.js today; the unified JS library and any future Go/Rust-side renderer driver) feeds each input through its own mapping pipeline and must produce the expected verdict WORD and display class. The tier law in one sentence: a value the server PUBLISHES is never browser-VERIFIED; presence maps to SERVER-ASSERTED, absence maps to NOT PROVEN (different honest states), and only local verification may mint PROVEN.

trunc_crashsafe.note: T-E3 (chipmunk ruling 2026-11-10): an absent field must never kill the page render. trunc() fails closed to this marker on null/undefined instead of throwing; renderSections over metadata with absent fields must complete, never throw. This is a page-death class, not cosmetics: the whole table is one synchronous render pass, so a throw is a dead page. Same property on BOTH surfaces (single-file bootproof.js + service-worker verify.js) and any future unified-library consumer.

render_sections_must_survive.note: metadata carrying the reachable absent fields (each reaches a trunc site); renderSections must return rows, never throw, and paint the marker.

must_include: verified in your browser by the service worker
rows marked SERVER-ASSERTED are published by the server and not attested
must_not_include_ci: every fact on this page was verified
